title: Quiet patch tactogram and ops notes — Nov 2026 (WIP)
content:
Purpose
A compact, low-noise rollout plan for the Nov patch to runtime-side prefix cache handling. Goal: ship a small safety-first change (KV edge-case fix) with minimal user-visible disruption, explicit rollback heuristics, and short watch windows. This is a working tactogram — terse, action-focused, notes-to-self style.

Scope
- Code: runtime cache eviction fix, small kernel selection tweak.
- Traffic: subset targeting internal beta + 5% prod traffic for 48 hours.
- Observability: token-level latency, error-rate per route, model-variant fallback rates.
- Excluded: bulk quantization and any config changes to autoscaler.

High-level calendar (compact)
- 2026-11-08 09:00 PT: Dry-run in staging (smoke + replay) — Lina leads.
- 2026-11-09 14:00 PT: Canary deploy to internal beta (10 hosts) — Theo runs.
- 2026-11-10 02:00 PT: Soft ramp to 5% prod (2h ramp) — Owen monitors.
- 2026-11-10 02:00–10:00 PT: Watch window 1 (aggressive sampling on tail latency).
- 2026-11-11 02:00–02:00 PT: Watch window 2 (24h stable) — if green, promote to 25% on 11/12.
- 2026-11-12 03:00 PT: Post-promote review + release notes cut.

Quick ops checklist (preflight)
- [ ] PR merged + CI green (no flaky tests) — owner: Maya.
- [ ] Canary image pushed to registry with tag quiet-patch-2026-11 — owner: Theo.
- [ ] Staging replay completed, no regressions on sample prompts — owner: Lina.
- [ ] Rollback image ready (previous stable tag) and rollback playbook verified — owner: Owen.
- [ ] Feature-gate flag created and validated (runtime.flag.quiet_patch) — owner: Maya.
- [ ] Oncall rota confirmed for 48h windows and escalation path is posted — owner: SRE Oncall.

Signal thresholds (alerting + manual abort gates)
- Latency: 99th token-latency increase > 20% vs baseline for 15m -> manual pause and investigate.
- Errors: request error-rate > 0.5% absolute increase over baseline for 10m -> rollback.
- Fallbacks: model-variant fallback rate > 2% (from variant A->B) for 30m -> roll back and disable flag.
- Memory: pod OOM occurrences > 0 in canary hosts -> immediate rollback.

Rollback matrix (fast decision table)
- Any of the above thresholds tripped during initial ramp -> immediate throttle to 0% (stop ramp) + switch to stable tag; notify #release-ops and Pager duty.
- Gradual increase but slowdowns in >1 region -> pause and restrict to region with low error until root cause known.

Telemetry snapshot plan (what we'll capture)
- Short-lived traces for sampled requests (include prompt length, model, route).
- Token-level latency distribution by route/model (1m rollup).
- KV cache hit/miss ratio and prefix eviction counts per host.
- Fallback mapping: which requests triggered variant fallback and why (metric and sample).
- Cost signal: token/call cost delta (quick sanity).

Release notes draft (proto language — to be cleaned)
- Title: Quiet patch: prefix cache edge-case fix and stability improvements (Nov 2026)
- Summary: Fixed an edge-case in the runtime prefix cache eviction that could cause higher-than-expected cache churn for certain long-context workloads. Deploy improves cache stability and reduces spiky tail latency for those routes. No model behavior changes expected.
- Impact: Small runtime change; short canary windows. Customers using very long sequences (>8k tokens) may see slightly lower 99p tail latency. No API or schema changes.
- Rollback strategy: automatic rollback to prior container image if telemetry thresholds are exceeded.
- Notes for customers: if you see any unexpected completions, contact support with request IDs (we'll add link).

Announcement draft (slack/email snippet)
- Slack (internal): "Quiet patch rolling today 02:00 PT -> 5% prod. Watch windows: 02:00–10:00 PT. Oncall: Owen, SRE Oncall. TL;DR: cache edge-case fix, low-risk. Ping @release-ops on anomalies."
- External (support template): "We deployed a maintenance patch addressing an internal cache stability issue; no API changes. If you notice regressions, please open a ticket and include request IDs."

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
- Should we extend canary to 48h if region-specific traffic shows transient blips? (decision needed before 11/10 01:00PT).
- Add a lightweight synthetic that exercises very long contexts to our smoke run (Lina).
- Confirm that the backup image has no newer infra libs that would confuse comparisons (Theo).
- Verify that the roll-forward path (hotpatch) is possible if rollback fails (Owen).

Runbook snippets (operator quick steps)
- Abort ramp: set runtime.flag.quiet_patch = off; scale down new deployment; switch target service selector to stable-tag; verify traffic drains from canaries; notify #release-ops with summary.
- Rollback quick check: check pod events for OOM; check KV eviction metric spikes; if OOMs -> rollback, else gather 1h trace and call SRE lead.

Postmortem triggers (fast rules)
- Trigger if any of: sustained 99p latency regression >20% for >1h; user-facing degradations reported by 3+ customers within 24h; rollback took >30m to complete.

Notes on communications and artifacts
- Post-promote: short post (internal) with link to telemetry snapshot and annotated grafana panels.
- Release notes will be merged into Confluence under /Release-Notes/2026/nov-quiet-patch.
- Link to PR and replay logs in linked_artifacts (above).

Quick retrospective prompts (after stability window)
- Did our thresholds catch regressions early enough?
- Was the watch team adequately staffed for the windows?
- Were rollback steps clear and fast?

Appendix: quick command cheats
- List canary pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=runtime,tag=quiet-patch-2026-11
- Force rollback (operator): kubectl -n inference set image deployment/runtime runtime=registry/redwood/runtime:stable-2026-10-21 && kubectl rollout status deployment/runtime

End of tactogram. Keep terse, iterate in comments below.

-- Maya

Quick edit log:
- 2026-11-03: initial sketch (Maya)
- 2026-11-05: added telemetry signals and thresholds (Lina)
- 2026-11-08: staged replay notes appended (Theo)
- 2026-11-10: tightened rollback matrix and added announcement drafts (Owen)
